statements.action_statement: No fixed release is available yet; update when Docker Hardened Images publishes one.
statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-124746 (Red Hat bug https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2571675): in BusyBox's volume_id code, volume_id_get_buffer() adds a 64-bit offset and length without checking for wraparound, so a crafted filesystem image can pass the buffer size check and make the NTFS prober read far outside the buffer, crashing blkid, findfs or mount LABEL=/UUID= when they probe devices. The Debian tracker lists busybox as unfixed in trixie with urgency unimportant ("Crash in CLI tool, no security impact"): https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-124746 . That is a decision not to ship a fix, not evidence that the code is absent. Upstream fixed it in commit https://github.com/vda-linux/busybox_mirror/commit/9387a70346e576d0fcc604e203381eecd58eace5 , which adds sanity checks throughout the NTFS prober in util-linux/volume_id/ntfs.c and an offset+length overflow check to volume_id_get_buffer() in util.c. That commit is not in a BusyBox release yet (the latest is 1.38.0), and DHI does not backport it. We checked /usr/bin/busybox in the busybox and busybox-static packages of all five published builds of 1:1.37.0-6+deb13u0, on amd64 and arm64, using the symbol tables in the -dbgsym packages: every one defines volume_id_probe_ntfs, volume_id_get_buffer, findfs_main and mount_main, the busybox package also defines blkid_main, and volume_id_get_buffer has the same size in every build of each package. Every published build of this owner is therefore affected.
